Subject: Apex - Renewal + Capacity Increase: MSA & Order Form (redlines)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, I’m following up with the renewal paperwork and the proposed capacity increase for Q3. High level:

- Term: 12 month renewal starting 2026-08-01 with the option to add 25% more reserved tokens at the same unit price for the first 90 days.
- Capacity: Requested +250k tokens/day baseline (see order form).
- Pricing: we’ve included the committed tier pricing that was discussed; incremental usage billed at on-demand rates.

I’m attaching our current MSA with our in-line redlines (Redwood_MSA_v3_EW_redlines.docx) and the draft Order Form (Apex_OrderForm_Q3_2026.pdf). Marcus and Laura are looped in for legal and procurement coordination.

Could you and your counsel review and highlight any material points? If Apex is okay with the term and capacity language in principle, we can prepare a mutual action plan and DocuSign flow for the order form while legal iterates on MSA items.

Next steps I propose:
1) Jordan — confirm the capacity numbers and whether the 90-day price-protection window works for you.
2) Apex legal — review the attached MSA redlines and flag any high-priority items (liability cap, data residency, termination for convenience).
3) Marcus/Laura — I’ll defer to you on acceptable counter-language and whether we need an executive sign-off for any concessions.

Thanks — want to keep this on a tight timeline so services aren’t interrupted.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Apex - Renewal + Capacity Increase: MSA & Order Form (redlines)

Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. We like the proposed capacity and the short price-protection window. A couple of items from our counsel that are likely to be sticking points:

- Auto-renew: our standard is automatic renewal unless 60 days notice is given. Can Redwood accept a 60-day notice instead of your 30?
- Liability cap: counsel is proposing a cap equal to 3x fees paid in the prior 12 months, excluding gross negligence.
- Data retention & residency: we need a clause that allows us to require data to be purged on termination and to restrict processing to US-only for regulated datasets.
- Sub-processing notice: requirement for 30 days notice before adding new sub-processors and the right to review security attestations.

I’ve attached Apex counsel’s marked-up MSA for your legal team to review (Apex_counsel_redlines.docx).

Can we set a call next week (Mon/Tue) to run through the high level and aim to close the order form by end of week? If you’re available Monday morning EDT that works for me.

Subject: Re: Apex - Renewal + Capacity Increase: MSA & Order Form (redlines)

Evelyn/Laura — thanks for tagging me. Quick read of Apex counsel redlines and my take:

Summary of positions and recommended responses:
- Auto-renew (60 days): we typically do 30-day notice. Compromise: agree to 60-day notice for auto-renew but include a 30-day optional early termination right for Redwood if capacity commitments are increased materially.
- Liability cap: 3x fees is above our standard; propose cap = 1x fees paid in prior 12 months with carveout for gross negligence and intentional misconduct. If finance signs off, we can flex to 2x for strategic/enterprise deals.
- Data residency & purge: can accept US-only processing for identified regulated workloads; require customer to designate datasets that need residency. Add explicit termination purge timeline (30 days) and certification of deletion within 45 days.
- Sub-processors: agree to 30 days notice and security attestation; decline right to veto (we can offer a 15-day review window and escalation to SOC reports).

Operational asks (order form / capacity):
- Need exact mapping: are the +250k tokens/day steady or burst? If burst, we should classify 200k baseline +50k burst and reflect in commitment and billing.
- Pricing: if Apex increases committed capacity by >20% mid-term, we should schedule an uplift review to adjust unit pricing at next invoice.

I’ve attached an internal response markup (MSA_response_markup.docx) with suggested language. My recommendation: schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call (Marcus + Kim) early next week to close the MSA language; Evelyn can run the commercial items (order form + DocuSign).

If Marcus and Kim agree, Laura/Finance, please confirm whether we can accept 2x liability cap as an escalated exception (we should flag for revenue operations).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_response_markup.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Apex - Renewal + Capacity Increase: MSA & Order Form (redlines)

Jordan / Kim — appreciate the quick turn from your side and thanks Marcus for the proposed counters.

Operational alignment: Apex’s +250k tokens/day looks to be steady-state based on the usage profile you shared; we’ll reflect that as 200k baseline + 50k burst in the order form to keep billing predictable.

Legal alignment (high level):
- Auto-renew: Redwood accepts 60-day notice (we’ll add a 30-day early termination right for material increases in committed capacity).
- Liability cap: Redwood can move to 2x fees paid in prior 12 months as a one-time exception for this renewal; this requires Revenue Ops sign-off and will be reflected in the order form summary.
- Data residency & purge: we can commit to US-only processing for designated regulated datasets and certify deletion within 45 days after termination.
- Sub-processors: Redwood will provide 30 days notice and recent SOC2 report; veto rights remain with Redwood, but we’ll provide a 15-day review window for security concerns.

Next steps:
1) Marcus and Kim — quick legal-to-legal call Monday 09:00 EDT to lock MSA redlines.
2) Jordan — once legal agrees, I’ll send the updated order form and DocuSign envelope.
3) Laura/Finance — can you confirm final approval on the 2x liability cap exception by EOD Monday so we can include it in the DocuSign package?

If that timeline works I’ll schedule the call and push the DocuSign link (placeholder: https://docusign.com/placeholder/APX-RNW-2026) and create the HubSpot deal update (HS-23456). Looking to close by 2026-07-02 to ensure capacity is in place for the start of the new term.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
